arguments.explanation: base1 has no registry spec block and thus no disturbance_tolerance_m of its own, so this is judged directly against the task's explicit requirement that base1, as the never-picked fixture, must never move. An observation-purpose monitor on base1 (agent-chosen 5mm threshold, since no registry threshold exists for this object) fired at 5.2mm displacement; querying base1's pose directly afterward showed a larger ~21mm translation and ~2.9deg rotation from its pose at run start -- well beyond anything attributable to TF noise. The placement frames derived from base1 (u_brown_placement) were observed to shift correspondingly between queries, corroborating that the fixture itself moved, not a sensor artifact. Believed mechanism: during the first place_u_brown attempt, u_brown came out of the approach/insertion motion misseated (12.96mm position error, ~27deg orientation error against u_brown_placement), landing tilted and in contact with base1's edge; that contact is ACM-permitted for planning but evidently transmitted enough force in simulation to shift the fixture. I did not reorder, abort, or otherwise change the plan because of this -- I proceeded to re-grasp and successfully reseat u_brown (now within tolerance, using the placement frame queried live after the shift, which is why the second placement is still correctly registered against wherever base1 now sits). This finding stands at run end as an uncorrected disturbance of the fixture itself, since there is no way to move base1 back (it is never picked and has no commanded target).
